decisions.reason: Clock has the lowest leave-trajectory-out error by a wide margin, while elapsed-time drift is visible across different input trials. Alternating maximizes disagreement with memory_clock.
decisions.prediction: During rapid input switches, clock predicts elapsed-time-dependent output even when input history changes; memory_clock may show additional history-dependent deviations.

decisions.reason: Clock has the lowest leave-trajectory-out error by a wide margin, and the alternating trial did not dislodge it. A second separated pulse can test whether elapsed-time forcing predicts responses despite changed input history.
decisions.prediction: The second pulse response will differ from the first according to elapsed time; a history-only model will predict a stronger dependence on prior pulse exposure.

decisions.reason: Clock has the best trajectory-level validation error, and both prior targeted trials had low forecast error without overturning it. PRBS provides varied input timing to test whether the remaining lag-correlated residuals reflect input history.
decisions.prediction: If clock is adequate, PRBS output will follow elapsed-time structure with little reproducible improvement from history-dependent models.
